title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
subtitle: Spiced and marinated Jamaican grilled chicken
excerpt: Jerk chicken is Jamaica's most famous dish -- chicken marinated in a fiery blend of allspice, scotch bonnet chilli, thyme, and aromatics, then grilled slowly over wood or charcoal. The result is deeply smoky, spicy, and fragrant. This is the definitive Caribbean barbecue.
sourceNotes: Jerk cooking was developed by the Maroons -- escaped enslaved Africans who hid in the mountains of Jamaica and used the jerk technique to preserve and cook wild pigs over slow fires of pimento (allspice) wood. Today jerk is sold at roadside shacks across Jamaica, particularly in Boston Bay, Portland, which is considered its spiritual home.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate overnight -- this is strongly recommended for the best flavour.
recipe.temperatureNote: For oven cooking; barbecue is preferable

content.text: Overnight marinating makes a real difference. The longer the chicken sits in the jerk paste, the deeper the flavour. Score the flesh right to the bone before marinating so the paste penetrates fully. If cooking on a barbecue, use indirect heat for the first 30 minutes.

items.prepNote: bone-in, skin-on -- scored deeply with a knife
or 1 scotch bonnet, seeds removed for less heat

content.text: Blend all the marinade ingredients together until smooth. Taste -- it should be very bold and spicy.
Score the chicken deeply with a sharp knife, cutting right to the bone. Coat all over with the jerk paste, pushing it into every cut.
Marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
To cook in the oven: preheat to 200 degrees. Place the chicken on a roasting tin. Cook for 45 to 50 minutes until the skin is dark and the chicken is cooked through.
To cook on a barbecue: place the chicken over indirect heat for 30 minutes, then move to direct heat for 10 to 15 minutes to char the skin.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving. Serve with rice and peas and fried plantain.

items.symptom: Marinade is not penetrating the meat
items.cause: Chicken was not scored deeply enough
items.fix: Score through the skin and into the flesh all the way to the bone -- this is the most important step

items.symptom: Chicken is burning outside before it is cooked through
items.cause: Sugar in the marinade caramelises quickly on high heat
items.fix: Start on lower or indirect heat for the first 30 minutes, then increase to finish

items.cause: Chilli flakes are much milder than fresh scotch bonnet
items.fix: Use a fresh scotch bonnet (seeds in) next time for authentic Jamaican heat

content.text: Jerk is Jamaica's gift to the world. Boston Bay in Portland parish is the jerk capital of Jamaica -- roadside shacks cook whole chickens and pork over smoking pimento wood pits. The combination of allspice and scotch bonnet is uniquely Caribbean. Jerk seasoning has now been adopted into cooking across the Caribbean, the UK, and North America.
